title: Chapter 5. Srimati Jahnava's Journey to Vrindavana
html:
Jahnava visits Ekachakra, Nityananda's birthplace (the story of the earring, kundala), and travels by way of Gaya, Kashi and Prayaga to Vrindavana; her meeting with Rupa and Sanatana and the wonder at Gopinatha's temple (pp. 45–50)

[p. 45]

1Glory, glory to Nityananda, honoured by Chaitanya!
Glory to Nityananda, the crown of all devotees1!

2Glory to Nityananda, the life of Vasu[dha] and Jahnava2!
Glory to Nityananda, deliverer of the lowly and the sinful!

3Glory to Virachandra, the son of Nityananda!
The merciful Virachandra is not different from Chaitanya.

4Now listen, all of you, to a wondrous account:
how the Prabhu3 set out for Vrindavana.

5Ramadasa, Ramai, Sundara and Jnanadasa4 —
these four the Prabhu called to her side.

6"In Radha, near Maureshvara, there is a village named Ekachakra5;
I wish to see the birthplace of my Prabhu.

7I must certainly go there — this is my wish."
"Very good, very good!" said the devotees.

8Saying "Sri Hari!", the Prabhu mounted her palanquin and set off;
the villagers, women and children, ran after her weeping.

9Some recalled the loving words the Prabhu had spoken to them:
no one in this life had shown them such affection6.

10Merciful in form, she was like Ganga, Sita and Lakshmi;
she had come to give her darshan to those she favoured with mercy.

11Whatever each one desired, he begged and received as a boon,
and all, grieving, went back to their homes.

12One mandal7, giving over his holdings to his children,
became a Vaishnava and went along with the Prabhu.

13His wife ran after him,
and a joyful cry of "Hari! Hari!" arose.

14Thus, step by step along the road, they came to a town,
stayed there one night and made great rejoicing.

15Then they came to the village of Ekachakra
and went to rest at Kundalitala8.

16All the brahmanas and good people who lived in that village
gathered together to see her.

17The son of a kinsman of the Pandita9, named Madhava,
came and showed her great honour.

18He gave the Vaishnavas fine lodgings
and saw separately to suitable food for each.

19He invited the Gosani to take rice in his own home10,
and the villagers went mad with joy.

20After the meal, in the evening, they began kirtana;
all the people, intoxicated, began to dance.

21Nityananda's Shakti displayed her power there11:
seeing the Gosani dance, all were amazed.

22Some saw all the serpents come up from the netherworld
and watch the dance, with jewels blazing on their heads.

23Others saw the gods in their aerial cars in the sky:
they too watched, while [the people] danced in the bliss of love.

[p. 46]

24"Hari bol! Bol Hari!" — crying "Hari!",
the people danced in the bliss of love with both arms raised.

25In this way two watches of the night passed12;
they closed the kirtana with the cry "Hari! Hari!".

26There the talk turned to the earring, the kundala;
Madhava told the story while all the devotees listened:

27"When Nityananda Prabhu took sannyasa,
he entered the avadhuta order and went naked.

28With a kundala in his ear and a staff in his hand
he wandered in all directions, visiting many holy places.

29After long wandering he came to his birthplace13
and arrived in this very village.

30At that time all the people of the village
were running away, with fear in their hearts.

31The Prabhu said, 'Where are you all running?'
All of them bowed down and told him:

32'A huge python has come into this village;
it causes great havoc and we are afraid of it.

33With cloths about our necks14 we pleaded with it:
"Why do you cause this havoc?

34You are the form of Ananta, pervading everything,
the destroyer and creator of the world, the protector of all."

35Then the python appeared and said to everyone:
"I will destroy all these living beings —

36unless you set up a turn from house to house
and bring me one offering every day."

37Hearing this, all the people in terror
resolved to leave the land and flee.'

38Hearing all this, the Prabhu laughed loudly
and, reassuring the villagers many times over, turned them back.

39On this very spot Nitai the avadhuta sat down
and looked about: where was the serpent?

40Here an opening of a burrow suddenly appeared15:
the great serpent, hood spread, came before him.

41The Prabhu seized its hood in his own hand
and murmured some mantra over it indistinctly.

42The serpent fell at his feet and slipped into its hole,
and the Prabhu closed the opening with the earring from his ear.

43This story spread from land to land,
and great crowds of people gathered round the Prabhu.

44For seven days the Prabhu rested here;
so the place came to be called Kundalitala, a great holy site.

45Since then the kundala grows day by day —
all the people of the village know this."

46Hearing this, all the devotees rejoiced:
such were the pastimes of Nityananda!

47Thus the avadhuta, wandering through the land,
delivered every region by giving his darshan.

48Nityananda Raya is equally merciful to all beings:
giving the name of Krishna, he delivers the world.

49The wicked, the slanderers, the heretics and the evil —
he draws all their hearts to himself by his virtues.

[p. 47]

50One who did not come to faith in such a Nityananda —
Providence turned away from him, and his life was wasted.

51When again, brothers, shall we have a human birth
to see Chaitanya and Nitai once more with our eyes?

52Even now, believe firmly,
and you will see the manifestation of the Prabhu's true form.

53Otherwise, like Jarasandha and Shishupala, you will not attain him16:
disgrace among men will be yours, and an evil end.

54One who, seeing and hearing so much, has not come to faith —
may that wretched one be ruined!

55If anyone, knowingly, reviles the Prabhu,
then I kick him on the head17.

56Glory, glory to Sri Krishna Chaitanya and Nityananda!
Be steadfast in devotion to the two brothers and you will find bliss.

57Hold Nityananda and Sri Chaitanya in your heart:
you will float in the bliss of love and be truly blessed.

58Thus in talk of the beloved the whole night
passed in great bliss, and they noticed nothing else.

59After the morning duties all bathed and gave gifts,
came to the Prabhu's feet and bowed down.

60Then the Prabhu departed from there
and came to the village of Ekachakra, the Prabhu's birthplace18.

61The village was wondrously beautiful, like Vrindavana;
seeing it, the Mother's heart rejoiced.

62How beautiful were all the trees, creepers and vines!
The people, devoted to Krishna, shone with radiance.

63How lovely was everything in the flower gardens!
Bees, drinking the nectar of the flowers, hummed.

64All the birds sang, maddened with love,
crying, "Glory to Nityananda and Krishna Chaitanya!"

65Seeing this, how Jahnava Devi rejoiced!
In her heart she knew it to be the hidden Shvetadvipa19.

66The Prabhu entered her own home20
with all her companions, joy in her heart.

67The Prabhu beheld Sri Bankima-deva21 —
and how she rejoiced together with the whole family!

68Gopijana-vallabha Prabhu22, his heart full of joy,
began a great sankirtana with the devotees.

69Hearing it, all the villagers rejoiced;
all said, "This is the Lord Himself in bodily form!"

70All cried "Blessed, blessed!" as they heard the kirtana —
women, children, the old and all the townsfolk.

71Now the Prabhu, steadfast in devotion to Bankima-deva,
himself performed his service with love.

72Thus some days passed in happiness:
every day a great festival and sankirtana, full of the rasa of bhakti.

73But the Mother, remembering Nityananda and Chaitanya,
was distressed by separation from the two Prabhus.

74"I will go to Vrindavana; there must be no delay" —
so Sri Jahnava reflected.

75The Prabhu called Gopijana-vallabha aside,
gave him the great mantra and taught him everything:

76the preaching of bhakti and the dharma of worship,
the path of the saints, the teaching of the books on bhakti, and the daily duties.

77She commanded: "Go back home.
I shall go to see Vrindavana-chandra.

78I can no longer bear the delay:
my heart is anxious for the Prabhu's darshan.

79Take the servants, maids and all the Vaishnavas with you;
become the guru of the world and teach it devotion.

[p. 48]

80Let Ramai and Sundarananda go with me,
four bearers for the palanquin and one maidservant."

81Hearing this, the Gosai23 fell down in a faint;
the Prabhu lifted him up with her holy hand.

82Taking him by the chin, she smelled his head24
and, imparting her own power to him, blessed him.

83Remembering "Krishna, Krishna!", the Mother of the world,
having performed service to Sri Bankima-deva Prabhu25,

84the Prabhu set out for Vrindavana,
and the Gosai, taking everyone, went back home.

85Thus Srimati Jahnava journeyed,
and everywhere she rescued people from their misfortunes.

86At her sight all things moving and unmoving thrilled;
wicked people kept aside in fear.

87Ramai went ahead, with all care,
making the way wherever they went.

88Step by step they came to holy Gaya;
on foot she came to the shrine of Vishnu26.

89Seeing the lotus feet of Vishnu, she was overcome with love;
all the brahmanas came to serve the Prabhu.

90Honouring them as brahmanas, she gave them gifts,
and for three nights she rested at holy Gaya.

91In the tall houses of the Gayalis, in fine lodgings27,
she fed the brahmanas sweets every day.

92Then she rested at Kashi,
beheld Vishveshvara and bathed in the Ganga.

93After staying three days at Kashi,
she went on, saying "Gauranga!", with bows and praises.

94Seeing the north-flowing Ganga28, she was glad,
and, saying "Krishna, Krishna!", the Prabhu went on to Prayaga.

95At Prayaga, seeing Madhava29, she was overcome with love,
and streams of tears flowed from both her eyes.

96Bathing at the Triveni, she felt great happiness;
she gave gifts to the brahmanas and greeted them.

97Bowing to Madhava with the words "Krishna, Krishna!",
she swayed in the rasa of love for Gaurachandra and Nityananda.

98Then the Mother departed from there,
crying again and again, "Ah, ah, Vrindavana-chandra!"

99Step by step they came to the land of Vrindavana;
there she left the palanquin and went on foot.

100Entering the land of Vraja, she prostrated herself,
and Lakshmi30 gazed her fill on the beauty of Vrindavana.

101Seeing Vrindavana, the Mother's love overflowed:
after a long time she had come to her own abode.

102"Where is the queen of my life, Srimati Radhika?
Where is the lord of my life, dearer to me than life?

103Where is Rama, where is Krishna?" — saying this,
the Mother was more and more overwhelmed with love.

104What she said, what she did — her mind was bewildered;
after a long while, regaining outer awareness, she wept.

105Restraining her emotion, she came to the temple;
all her companions cried, "Hari bol!"

106Ramai went into the temple and gave word of her coming;
hearing it, the Vaishnavas went mad with joy.

107The Vaishnavas of Vrindavana, Rupa and Sanatana31,
fell prostrate at the Prabhu's feet.

[p. 49]

108"Where is my mother Kirtida, my father Vrishabhanu?
Where is my mother Vrajeshvari, where is Rohini Devi?"32 —

109thus, immersed in the rasa of Vraja-love,
she lay motionless in the madness of love.

110The Queen of Vrindavana revealed her own radiance33:
all Vrindavana saw a splendour like lightning.

111In the Prabhu they saw the Queen of Vrindavana herself —
the same dress, the same lustre as the daughter of Vrishabhanu.

112Seeing this, Rupa and Sanatana were astonished,
and the two brothers fainted before the Prabhu.

113Seeing them, the teacher of the world, the mother of the world,
the Mother gave them both her blessing.

114"Rise, rise," the Mother began to say.
Rising, Rupa and Sanatana joined their palms,

115and Rupa and Sanatana together recited praises,
and the Vaishnavas were plunged in an ocean of bliss:

116"You are Hari's beloved, you are the teacher of the world;
whatever anyone asks, he receives: you are the wish-fulfilling tree.

117You are the Queen of Vrindavana, the giver of devotion to Krishna;
you are the chief of the spiritual energies (chit-shakti), you are the mother of the world.

118Apart from you Krishna has no dearer beloved;
Krishna tastes the rasa of joy from you."

119Thus the two brothers offered many praises;
hearing them, the Mistress of the world was pleased.

120Then the Mother said to Rupa and Sanatana:
"Seeing you both, my heart is moved with compassion.

121You two are recipients of my Prabhu's favour;
you are both full of loving devotion, you are pure sattva."

122The Mother cast an auspicious glance on everyone,
and all rejoiced and counted themselves fortunate.

123Mukhya Haridasa34 and Gosai Dasa Pujari
brought a tray filled with the garland of permission35 and prasada.

[p. 50]

124Receiving the prasada and the garland, the Mother bowed
and accepted them with the deepest devotion.

125[…] she went toward the temple36;
people going ahead opened the doors.

126Crying "Gopinatha!", she went with ardent love,
and at that very moment the Prabhu entered the holy shrine.

127Unblinking she gazed on the beautiful moon-faced [form];
she could say nothing, only her lips trembled.

128Suddenly the doors of the shrine closed —
no one could understand what play he was performing.

129Gopinatha, drawing Jahnava by her garment,
took her and seated her at his left side.

130Fair-faced Radha rejoiced:
two beloveds on either side — who can tell such beauty!

131All were utterly amazed;
the temple servants went and opened the doors.

132All see her, become a golden image,
seated at Gopinatha's left37.

133Astonished, all gazed on this;
Gopinatha's face was radiant with joy.

134On the left Sri Jahnava, on the right Radhika,
Gopinatha in the middle — what comparison could surpass it?

135Nityananda and Gopinatha are one body:
the Dialogue of the Earth and Shesha38 proclaims this aloud.

136Nityananda is Gopinatha, Jahnava is Ananga,
and Radhika, Ananga's elder sister, is the beloved of Sri Krishna39.

137Ananga is Rama's female body:
for Radhika's happiness she stays with Krishna.

138Chaitanya is the descent of Radha and Krishna in one form;
Rama-Nityananda shares in his play.

139He who is Rama is Krishna, is Gaurachandra;
Sri Radhika and Sri Jahnava are Ananga [and] Nityananda40.

140One reality manifests in different forms:
to taste the pastimes, it plays in this way.

141Whatever pastime Krishna desires in his heart,
taking that form Rama plays together with Krishna.

142Who can understand Rama's pastimes, endless and boundless?
Both the male and the female principle are none other than Rama.

143Bringing majesty and sweetness with them,
Gaura and Nityananda, appearing in Navadvipa,

144all descend and distribute love;
in Vrindavana they play together in union.

145Thus the Lord's pastimes have no interruption:
the Vedas speak only of appearance and disappearance.

146The feet of Sri Jahnava and Nityananda Prabhu —
they are my refuge in life and in death.

147Hoping for the feet of Virachandra Prabhu,
Vrindavana Dasa tells the Spreading of the Lineage.

Thus ends the fifth chapter, named "Sri Srimati [Jahnava]'s Journey to Vrindavana", in the Madhya-lila of the Spreading of the Lineage of Sri Sri Nityananda Prabhu.

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. The line is badly corrupted in both copies ("savva bhakti śirodhārya"); read as "sarva bhakta śirodhārya", "crown of all devotees".
  2. The copies have "vanu"/"vastu"; read as "vasu" (Vasu, i.e. Vasudha): "the life of Vasudha and Jahnava", Nityananda's two wives.
  3. "Prabhu" ("Mistress, Sovereign") in this chapter usually means Jahnava Devi, who is also called "the Mother" (Mata); the Bengali verbs do not mark gender, so the reference is clear only from context. Nityananda himself is also "the Prabhu" ("my Prabhu", "the Prabhu's birthplace").
  4. Jahnava's companions. Sundara is Sundarananda (cf. couplet 80); Ramai is probably Ramachandra (Ramai), Jahnava's adopted son.
  5. Radha (Rarh) is the region west of the Ganga. Maureshvara (mauṛaeśvara) is a locality in present Birbhum district, near Ekachakra.
  6. The couplet is obscure ("keha keha prabhu yevā prīti vākya vaila / e janame yena līlā eta sneha kaila"); translated by the general sense.
  7. A mandal is a village headman holding a hereditary allotment (vritti).
  8. Kundalitala, "the place of the kundala (earring)", a holy spot in Ekachakra; its name is explained below, couplets 26–45.
  9. The Pandita is probably Hadai Pandita, Nityananda's father; Madhava is the son of one of his kinsmen.
  10. "Ghar-bhat", rice cooked at home, i.e. a meal in his own house. "Gosani" is a respectful address for Jahnava.
  11. Nityananda's Shakti (energy, consort) is Jahnava.
  12. Two watches (praharas): about six hours, i.e. until midnight.
  13. The Chaitanya-bhagavata (Adi, ch. 8) also says that Nityananda visited his birthplace while wandering as an avadhuta.
  14. Tying a cloth about the neck is a gesture of humble supplication.
  15. The copies have "viṣadvāra/vṣidvāra"; read as "vivara dvāra", "the opening of a burrow".
  16. Jarasandha and Shishupala were enemies of Krishna. The words "nā pāive" ("you will not attain") follow the copies; the sense is "do not be like them".
  17. An echo of a well-known line of the Chaitanya-bhagavata: "then I kick him on the head".
  18. They had earlier stopped at Kundalitala; now Jahnava comes to the very house where Nityananda was born.
  19. Shvetadvipa, the "White Island", a divine abode of Vishnu; here Ekachakra is understood as the hidden Shvetadvipa.
  20. Nityananda's house is "her own" as the house of her husband.
  21. Bankima-deva (Bankima Raya), the deity of Krishna at Ekachakra.
  22. Gopijana-vallabha is apparently a member of the family (according to some sources a son of Virachandra); Jahnava leaves him at Ekachakra and initiates him (couplets 75–79). The "Prabhu" serving Bankima-deva in couplet 71 is apparently he.
  23. The Gosai here is Gopijana-vallabha.
  24. Smelling the head is a traditional gesture of parental affection and blessing.
  25. "Mother of the world" (jagan-mata) is an epithet of Jahnava; she is the subject of couplets 83–84 and herself serves the Deity before departing.
  26. The copies have "pada eje … viṣṇudyāne"; read as "padavraje … viṣṇusthāne". The shrine of Vishnu at Gaya is the Vishnupada temple with the footprint of Vishnu.
  27. The Gayalis are the hereditary priests of Gaya; the copies have "gadhā~laẏa]/gāla ghara", read as "Gayali houses".
  28. At Kashi (Varanasi) the Ganga flows north (uttara-vahini), which is considered especially auspicious.
  29. Madhava is the deity Veni-Madhava at Prayaga (Allahabad); the Triveni is the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and Sarasvati.
  30. Lakshmi here is Jahnava.
  31. Rupa and Sanatana Gosvamis. The editor notes the chronological difficulty: by the usual chronology they were no longer living at the time of Jahnava's journey to Vrindavana.
  32. Jahnava speaks as Ananga Manjari, Radha's younger sister: Kirtida and Vrishabhanu are Radha's parents; Vrajeshvari is Yashoda, Krishna's mother; Rohini is Balarama's mother.
  33. The copies read "nija bhā", "her own radiance" (Skt. bha), rhyming with "ābhā".
  34. "Mukhya Haridasa", "the chief (priest) Haridasa"; the editor takes him to be Haridasa Pandita, the servant of Govinda-deva. Gosai Dasa Pujari served the deity Madana-mohana.
  35. The garland of permission (ajna-mala) is the deity's garland sent to a guest as a sign of blessing and leave.
  36. The first word of the line is illegible (A "grādarana", B "śrī-rana").
  37. The tradition that Jahnava, entering Gopinatha's temple, merged into the deity; an image of Jahnava stands beside Gopinatha in Vrindavana.
  38. The Dialogue of the Earth and Shesha (Dharani-Shesha-samvada), a text attributed to the Brahmanda Purana; it is quoted in ch. 6.
  39. Ananga Manjari is Radha's younger sister; in the Nityananda tradition Jahnava is held to be her incarnation.
  40. The line is given as in the copies ("śrīrādhikā śrījāhnavā anaṅga nityānanda"); the poet does not make the pairing (Radhika with Gaura; Jahnava, Ananga, Nityananda) explicit.
